algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide that covers everything you need to turn a design concept into a fully‑functional, production‑ready e‑commerce front‑end. Feel free to skip sections that already match your current setup – the goal is to give you a clear “roadmap” you can follow or adapt. --- ## 1️⃣ Planning & Design | Step | What to do | Why it matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **Define goals** | List core features (product catalog, cart, checkout, search, filters, reviews, admin panel, etc.). | Keeps scope focused. | | **Create user personas** | Identify target shoppers (e.g., “budget buyer”, “tech enthusiast”). | Drives UX decisions. | | **Sketch wireframes** | Low‑fidelity sketches of key pages (home, category, product, cart, checkout). | Visualise layout early. | | **Build a prototype** | Use Figma/Adobe XD/Sketch → interactive prototype. | Validate flow before coding. | | **Design system** | Define colors, typography, spacing, component library. | Consistency & reusability. | > **Tip:** Keep a shared design file (Figma) so developers can inspect CSS values directly. --- ## 2️⃣ Choose a Tech Stack | Layer | Suggested Tech | Why | |-------|----------------|-----| | **Framework** | **Next.js** (React + SSR/SSG) | SEO, fast first paint, built‑in API routes. | | **Language** | **TypeScript** | Compile‑time safety, better IDE support. | | **Styling** | **Tailwind CSS** + **Headless UI** | Rapid styling, utility‑first, no CSS bloat. | | **State** | **Zustand** or **Redux Toolkit** | Simple global store for cart, auth, etc. | | **Data fetching** | **React Query** or **SWR** | Caching, background refetch, optimistic updates. | | **Payments** | **Stripe Elements** | PCI‑compliant, easy checkout UI. | | **Auth** | **NextAuth.js** | OAuth, email magic links, JWT, session handling. | | **Testing** | **Jest + React Testing Library**, **Cypress** | Unit + E2E coverage. | | **Storybook** | **Storybook** | Component isolation & documentation. | | **Deployment** | **Vercel** (or Netlify) | Zero‑config, automatic preview URLs. | | **CI/CD** | **GitHub Actions** | Run tests, lint, build, deploy on push. | > **Alternative**: If you prefer Vue, swap Next.js → Nuxt 3, React Query → Vue Query, etc. --- ## 3️⃣ Development Workflow ### 3.1 Project Setup ```bash npx create-next-app@latest my-ecommerce --typescript cd my-ecommerce npm i tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p ``` Add Tailwind to `globals.css`: ```css @tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities; ``` ### 3.2 Folder Structure ``` /components # Reusable UI pieces /pages # Next.js pages (home, product, cart, etc.) /lib # API helpers, auth utils /store # Zustand/Redux slices /styles # Tailwind config, global styles /utils # Helpers (formatting, validation) ``` ### 3.3 Core Components #### Product Card (React + Tailwind) ```tsx // components/ProductCard.tsx import Image from 'next/image'; import Link from 'next/link'; export interface ProductCardProps { id: string; title: string; price: number; imageUrl: string; } export const ProductCard: React.FC = ({ id, title, price, imageUrl, }) => (

{title}

${price.toFixed(2)}

 ); ``` #### Cart Store (Zustand) ```ts // store/cart.ts import create from 'zustand'; interface CartItem { productId: string; quantity: number; } interface CartState { items: CartItem[]; addItem: (item: CartItem) => void; removeItem: (productId: string) => void; clearCart: () => void; } export const useCartStore = create((set) => ({ items: [], addItem: (item) => set((state) => ({ items: [...state.items, item], })), removeItem: (productId) => set((state) => ({ items: state.items.filter((i) => i.productId !== productId), })), clearCart: () => set({ items: [] }), })); ``` ### 3.4 API Integration Use `react-query` to fetch products: ```tsx // lib/api.ts export const fetchProducts = async () => { const res = await fetch('/api/products'); if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Network response was not ok'); return res.json(); }; ``` ```tsx // pages/index.tsx import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'; import { ProductCard } from '@/components/ProductCard'; export default function Home() { const { data, isLoading, error } = useQuery(['products'], fetchProducts); if (isLoading) return

Loading…

; if (error) return

Error loading products.

; return (
{data.map((p) => ( ))}
); } ``` ### 3.5 Checkout Flow 1. **Cart page** – show items, allow quantity changes, remove items. 2. **Checkout page** – collect shipping address, payment method. 3. **Stripe Elements** – embed card input, handle tokenization. 4. **Serverless API route** (`/api/checkout`) – create a Stripe Checkout Session. 5. **Redirect** to Stripe’s hosted checkout or confirm payment client‑side. --- ## 4️⃣ Testing | Tool | Purpose | Example | |------|---------|---------| | **Jest + RTL** | Unit tests for components | `expect(screen.getByText('Add to cart')).toBeInTheDocument()` | | **Cypress** | End‑to‑end tests | `cy.visit('/products/123').click('[data-testid=add-to-cart]')` | | **Storybook** | Isolated component docs | `storiesOf('Button').add('primary', () => )` | > **CI**: Add a GitHub Action that runs `npm run lint && npm run test && npm run build`. --- ## 5️⃣ Deployment & CI/CD ```yaml # .github/workflows/deploy.yml name: Deploy on: push: branches: [main] jobs: build-and-deploy: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 - uses: actions/setup-node@v3 with: node-version: '20' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run test - run: npm run build - uses: vercel/action@v1 with: vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }} vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID }} ``` > **Secrets**: Store API keys, Stripe secret, Vercel token in GitHub Secrets. --- ## 6️⃣ Performance & Accessibility | Area | Recommendation | |------|----------------| | **Image optimization** | Use Next.js `Image` component, serve WebP/AVIF, lazy‑load. | | **Code splitting** | Automatic with Next.js; use dynamic imports for heavy libs. | | **Lazy loading lists** | `react-window` for long product lists. | | **Accessibility** | `aria-label`, semantic HTML, focus management, color contrast ≥ 4.5:1. | | **SEO** | Server‑rendered pages, meta tags, structured data (JSON‑LD). | | **Analytics** | Google Analytics, Plausible, or Matomo. | | **Error tracking** | Sentry for runtime errors. | | **Performance audit** | Lighthouse, Web Vitals. | --- ## 7️⃣ Security Checklist | Item | How to implement | |------|------------------| | **HTTPS** | Vercel automatically provides SSL. | | **CORS** | Configure API routes to accept only your domain. | | **CSRF** | Use SameSite cookies or CSRF tokens. | | **XSS** | Escape all user‑generated content, use DOMPurify for rich text. | | **Rate limiting** | Cloudflare Workers or API gateway. | | **Auth** | NextAuth.js with JWT + refresh tokens. | | **Payment** | Stripe Elements + server‑side webhook validation. | | **Secrets** | Store in environment variables, never commit. | --- ## 8️⃣ Maintenance & Monitoring | Tool | Use case | |------|----------| | **Sentry** | Runtime error alerts. | | **Datadog / New Relic** | Performance metrics, uptime monitoring. | | **GitHub Actions** | Automated lint, test, build on PRs. | | **Vercel Analytics** | Real‑time traffic insights. | | **Google Search Console** | Indexing health, crawl errors. | --- ## 9️⃣ Next Steps 1. **Prototype** → get stakeholder approval. 2. **Set up repo** → add CI/CD, linting, formatting. 3. **Implement core pages** → home, product, cart, checkout. 4. **Add admin panel** (optional) → manage inventory, orders. 5. **Deploy** → preview URLs for stakeholders. 6. **Iterate** → gather feedback, add features (reviews, wishlists, recommendations). --- ### Quick Reference: `package.json` Scripts ```json { "scripts": { "dev": "next dev", "build": "next build", "start": "next start", "lint": "eslint . --ext .ts,.tsx", "test": "jest", "storybook": "start-storybook -p 6006", "build-storybook": "build-storybook" } } ``` --- ## 🎉 Final Thought Building a front‑end for an e‑commerce site is a marathon, not a sprint. Start small, iterate fast, and keep the user experience at the center. With the stack above, you’ll have a modern, maintainable, and scalable foundation that can grow with your business. Happy coding! 🚀
